what: A chocolate film (WebGL) covering the board first sweeps in from the left in .7s, and drops grow from the bottom edge in fifteen strands. From 1.3s the film lifts upward over 2.1s with power2.inOut — drop tips trail the film by .16 to .46s, stretching into long strands before snapping, and in the last 14% they rise a further .387 of the board height and leave the screen. The title on the film (child of title) rises together with the film. The shader draws the vertical grain like folded cloth and the bead light on the edges

options.dur: Overall curtain clock (seconds), default 5.5 — substitute clock for the original chroma-key video
options.sweep: Length in seconds of the cover coming in from the left, default .7 — at 0 it is covered from the start
options.[data-fx-part=title]: Title that rides up together over the curtain (if any)
options.--fx-drip · --fx-drip-lit: Dark film color · light grain color (default --kf-ink · half --kf-ink and half --kf-bg)

from.where: stage.js chocolate curtain shader — original hero chroma-key video (clock 5.5s · offset −.387 cubed during the final 14% · bag drops at start .001 · head visible at .5)

note: When finished, data-drip-done is added to the element and an fx-done event fires. While covering the panel it does not block interaction (pointer-events none). Without WebGL, it goes straight to the finished state with no overlay
